messages:
maria: FYI — eu-central GPU fleet is degraded, we’re seeing ~70% of GPU pods NotReady after node image rollout failed. High token queues and increased 502s. Not sure if networking or driver mismatch yet.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] incident created #INC-2026-1345 — paging oncall-sre

kevin_sre: investigating. nodes show kubelet OOM and nvidia-driver errors in dmesg. Rolling back image on a small subset to confirm.

ash_ops: adding tags: impacting-hosted, impact=high, affected-region=eu-central

maria: current traffic: bursts are queuing on frontend, causing per-req latency to spike. We need emergency throttles until we have capacity.

jordan_sales: we have 3 enterprise customers with SLAs in eu1. Any plan to avoid breaking them? Need to protect reserved capacity.

kevin_sre: plan: 1) enable per-customer soft throttles (rate limit by rps + token budget) 2) re-route non-enterprise traffic to us-west1 fallbacks with degraded perf 3) roll back node image for remaining nodes 4) gradual restore

lee_runtime: I can push a config that enforces per-customer token-bucket limits via the edge rate-limiter (envoy + rate-limiter). Suggest rules:

``
match: customer.tier == "free" => rps: 5, burst: 20
match: customer.tier == "standard" => rps: 20, burst: 50
override: customer.tags contains "enterprise" => rps: 200, bypass_quota: true
``

kevin_sre: that looks good. Also add a global per-tenant token cap of 10k tokens/minute to reduce KV cache pressure.

ash_ops: I can flip the feature flags. Command to push (internal):

``
curl -X POST https://internal-control.redwood/v1/edge/rate-limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"rules": [...], "region": "eu-central", "mode":"emergency"}'
``

maria: do it but DO NOT block enterprise. We need explicit allowlist for enterprise-account ids: E-1001, E-1002, E-1017

jordan_sales: confirmed — please whitelist E-1001 and E-1002. E-1017 on support call, ok to throttle lightly but notify.

lee_runtime: pushing rules now in gradual rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Watch logs. Patch applied: rollout id rl-2026-998

ops_jen: seeing edge pods apply config. Starting to see immediate drop in queue depth on frontends (−30%). Good signal.

kevin_sre: rolling back nodes batch-2 now: `kubectl rollout undo ds/gpu-node-daemonset --to-revision=3 -n infra` — monitoring driver statuses

maria: traffic shift to us-west1 for non-enterprise started. Note: latency will increase for EU customers routed out-of-region. Please prep comms.

product_emma: prepping banner: "We’re experiencing degraded capacity in eu-central. If you’re on free/standard tiers you may see rate limits or increased latency. Enterprise customers are prioritized." Drafted, will publish after confirmation.

jordan_sales: also message customers E-1017 and E-1002 via support. E-1001 is on a production job right now — we must avoid interruption.

kevin_sre: status: node rollback healthy on 30% of nodes, driver kernel oops reduced. Still ~40% nodes rebuilding. Token queues trending down.

ash_ops: cost note: shifting traffic to us-west1 will incur cross-region egress; logged ticket FIN-289 to track emergency spend.

oncall-bot: [UPDATE] incident INC-2026-1345 — emergency throttles applied, rollback in progress, traffic shift started

maria: decision log: enable emergency per-customer throttles in eu-central (free/standard reduced), whitelist enterprise ids, route overflow to us-west1, rollback node image. Postmortem owner: kevin_sre, initial severity: P1.

kevin_sre: next steps: continue rollback, verify KPIs (p95 latency, 502 rate, token queue length). If no improvement in 30m, escalate to infra-leads for capacity reallocation.

ash_ops: creating temp dashboards for token usage and per-customer throttles. Link: http://grafana.internal/d/edge/emergency-eu-central

maria: thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. I'll coordinate customer comms once we confirm impact windows.
